content.title: How Deontay Wilder beat Derek Chisora on split decision in titanic heavyweight fight
content.text: Deontay Wilder marked his 50th fight with a split-decision victory over Derek ChisoraDeontay Wilder beat Derek Chisora via split decision in his first career fight in London. Getty ImagesWilder beats Chisora via split decision in 50th career fightDeontay Wilder marked his 50th professional fight with a split-decision victory over Derek Chisora after 12 brutal rounds in London.The two veterans of the heavyweight decision traded countless blows and it was the American who shaded his British opponent, knocking him down twice while only being put down once himself.Two judges scored the fight in favour of Wilder (115-111 and 115-113) while the other scored it in favour of Chisora (115-112).After the fight, Wilder voiced his intention to follow up this evening's victory with a world title fight.Share your thoughts: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementChisora not drawn on retirement decision It was a night of what ifs for Derek Chisora who will be running the fight back through his head as he tries to get to sleep this evening — here is what he had to say to DAZN in the ring afterwards.💬 “Some of the rounds were very close. I'm upset, If I didn't come onto the ropes, I would've won the fight. It happens. The fight, I lost it by two points because I came out of the ring. It is what it is.”The next question Chisora faced was whether this evening's defeat marked the end of his boxing career.“I'm going to go home with the boss lady (his wife) and see. I'm going to go home and drop the kids (off), do the school run.”A world-title fight feels beyond Wilder despite Chisora win Getty ImagesI don't mean to take anything away from Deontay Wilder's victory this evening — any win at this level given the risk associated — but it doesn't feel like he is close to where he needs to be to challenge for a world title.It was a gutsy performance this evening full of heart and he has said that he will only get better, but I can't see how he would break down a fighter as good as Oleksandr Usyk. We have to remember that Wilder was knocked by a 42-year-old Derek Chisora this evening.I would, however, love to see Wilder get in the ring with Anthony Joshua next. That is a fight that has the potential to be an absolute cracker.Wilder: 'I'm back and I'll get better and better' Getty ImagesDeontay Wilder had plenty to say in the ring to DAZN after the fight, starting with a message to his doubters.💬 “Many people doubted me, they counted me out, they threw dirt on my name. You can’t throw dirt on someone who has shovelled it. Y’all were witness today about what destiny is all about.“I thank Derek. Bro, we have to go fishing. Come to Alabama baby.”He was then asked if he wants a run at a world-title fight.“Most definitely, hands down. Tonight was fun, I was having a lot of fun. Derek got a lot of good shots off but I’m a king and I showed that tonight. I came back, it was about coming back. I had to heal. But I’m back and I’ll get better and better each time.”Tonight's results in full Getty ImagesDeontay Wilder def. Derek Chisora via split decisionViddal Riley def. Mateusz Masternak via unanimous decisionDenzel Bentley def.. Endry Saavedra via R7 TKOMatty Harris def. Franklin Ignatius via R2 KOAmir Anderson def. Jordan Dujon via R8 TKOChisora went out to a hero's ovation I know he will be paid an eye-watering sum for this evening's fight, but I will never know how a man can put himself through all that at the age of 42.The writing looked to be on the wall for Derek Chisora after two rounds yet he managed to drag himself through 12 rounds and even gave himself a chance of winning the fight after battling back time and again.It was a real shame, for Chisora and his home crowd, that he wasn't able to summon the power to knock Wilder out but a late knockdown was a fine consolation for his efforts.If that is the last we have seen of the Brit in the boxing ring, then we must be thankful for what he has given us across his 19-year career.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementLook at what it means to Deontay Wilder! Getty ImagesWhether it is your first fight or your 50th, that feeling of winning a heavyweight fight remains the same!Lots of questions were asked about Wilder coming into this evening and, while he didn't answer all of them, that victory must feel so sweet.What comes next is a question for another time but, for now, the 40-year-old can enjoy the 45th win of his career.A successful first visit to London for Wilder It was hard to believe that Deontay Wilder had waited until the 50th fight of his career to make his London debut — and what a spectacle it was!The American expected plenty of love from the crowd inside the O2 Arena but ended up playing the pantomime villain after edging Derek Chisora via split decision.If he does extend his career beyond this evening, I'm sure he'd love to come back. The big question for Derek Chisora after the fight was whether he would go again after going 12 rounds with Deontay Wilder, but he would not be drawn on whether tonight was the last time we have seen him in the ring.I'm sure his decision, whatever his decision is, will come after he has recovered, taken stock and worked out whether it is worth to get himself in fighting condition.Tremendous respect between the fightersAs we have seen throughout this fight week, there was enormous respect shown between the fighters in the ring afterwards.Deontay Wilder offered Derek Chisora the opportunity to visit him in Alabama to go fishing. Though the American wasn't fooling anyone when he followed that up by saying he went easy on the Brit.Lastly, Wilder finished with a message to his children: “I'm coming home!” Getty ImagesWilder brought what he had left in him out tonight. The power was still there, perhaps not the killer instinct to finish Chisora when he was hurt, although the Brit is a survival specialist. Wilder edges Chisora by a majority decision but, in truth, the 'Bronze Bomber' is likely to fall short if he steps up the calibre of opposition again. Chisora is set to bring the curtain down on a fantastic career and put on a performance that was typical of the fighter the British boxing public love.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementWilder wins via split decision! Getty ImagesSo, let's see how the three judges scored it.115-111 to Wilder.115-112 to Chisora.115-113 Wilder.The American wins via split decision which, for me, is a fair outcome.Either way, that was brilliant entertainment even if it lacked the technical brilliance that boxing purists would like to see.To the judges ... Getty ImagesI have to agree with Chris.Wilder seemed to connect with a lot more of his shots throughout that fight — he started the brighter and finished the better, for me.Chisora scrapped his way back into the fight and was the better fighter for a spell in the middle of the fight, but I don't think he's done enough to get the win.Over to the judges we go ... I don't envy them having to score that fight one bit! Round 12: Chisora 9-10 WilderAnother scrappy final round in a slugfest of a fight which Wilder probably just did enough to win with some cleaner shots. The American is the winner on my card.Chisora 111-115 Wilder Getty ImagesA really entertaining fight between two veterans. The song “Forever Young” by Alphaville plays, again suitably, at the final bell. Two fighters, in their 50th fights respectively, slugging it out until the end. Both vulnerable, both chaotic. Chisora vs. Wilder round twelve Getty ImagesPerhaps the last three minutes of both of these fighters' careers — can either of them raise the roof with a knockout?Chisora, still fuelled by his late knockdown in the last round, goes on the front foot but is soon on his way back to the ropes after a smart combination from Wilder.The Brit goes for the killer blow in the last few seconds of the final round, but can't connect and the fight ends with both men hugging on the ropes.A brilliant, old-school heavyweight fight is brought to an end with everyone inside the O2 Arena on their feet.I'm not quite sure how that lasted the distance — how on earth do you score it?SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement Round 11: Chisora 9-10 WilderGood jabs from Wilder to start the round and a nice loose right hand which were important scoring shots. Chisora did go to the body well again but the bigger shots were coming from the American which, on my card, means the British fighter needs a knock out. Chisora was out of the ring, Wilder was down but neither counted as knockdowns.Chisora 102-105 WilderChisora vs. Wilder round eleven Getty ImagesIs this the round Wilder puts Chisora away?Not quite, but there is a count! Chisora, who has more body out of the ring than inside it, scampers to get back inside.And then he knocks Wilder down for the first time in the fight! The American is straight back to his feet, but is facing a swell of noise and the charging advances of Chisora.The bell sounds a few seconds later and Wilder has the break between rounds to compose himself.Don't rule out a final-round knockout! Getty ImagesBoth down in the 11th! After Chisora’s corner were unhappy that Chisora, falling out of the ring for a third time, was ruled a knockdown instead of a slip, things evened themselves out after Chisora’s clubbing shots knocked Wilder down. The American grinned but this is a dogfight that has taken a lot out of both men. Round 10: Chisora 10-9 WilderA good left to the head was followed to the body from Wilder at the start of the 10th and Chisora backed off, standing in the corner trying to lure in the American while blocking right hands. Chisora landed a good right at the end of the round but enough to nick it.Chisora 93-95 Wilder
